answer.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 shows activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—directly addressing the current activation decline. Memory_31 demonstrated that simplifying signup improved first-week activation. Together these suggest the issue may not be onboarding friction itself but rather engagement post-onboarding. Activation_messaging is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed retention harm) and doesn't require the established customer base that referral_incentives depend on. Enterprise_sales_assist won't address the SMB activation decline or help against price-sensitive competitor pressure. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging allows us to verify the tactic works in current conditions while preserving optionality for follow-up moves (like simplified onboarding if messaging alone is insufficient). Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the magnitude of prior gains and any decay.
